title_original: Top Agencies Lead New Coalition To Push For U.S. Indie Production

blocks.text: A group of talent agencies and producers have joined forces to create to the American Entertainment Alliance dedicated to promoting U.S. independent production. The new coalition will push for legislation requiring major studios and streamers to allocate half of their original content budgets to indie production.

Founding members include CAA , WME , UTA , Anonymous Content, Blumhouse, CAA, Imagine Entertainment, Jeff Sagansky, Legendary Entertainment, MRC, North Road, Producers United, Propagate Content and Ziffren Brittenham.

The AEI is focused on strengthening competition, expanding opportunities for indie producers and creators, and supporting film and TV production in the U.S., addressing a fundamental restructuring of the entertainment business. Studio consolidation and streaming have dramatically narrowed the market for independent content, disrupting the economics of film and TV, said UTA on Instagram today, noting it’s “proud to be a member of the American Entertainment Alliance”

blocks.text: The AEA will advocate for modern creative ownership rules that reflect today’s streaming marketplace and support policies that make the United States more competitive as a production destination.
“As film and television increasingly consolidate, we need a regulatory framework that puts creators first, protects industry workers and preserves competition,” said UTA’s Vice Chair Jay Sures.
The Alliance was first reported in the New York Times.
